**Verse 19–21 (Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi, *Zad al-Masir*)**

God's words: ﴿So know that there is no god but God﴾. Some said: "Remain steadfast upon your knowledge." Others said: "The address in this is intended for someone other than him. We have explained this at the beginning of *al-Ahzab* (the chapter of the Confederates)." It was also said: "He used to feel distress in his chest because of what they said, so it was said to him: Know that there is no remover of what is upon you except God."

As for His words: ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, he used to seek forgiveness one hundred times a day. He was commanded to ask forgiveness for the believing men and women, as an honour to them, because he is an intercessor whose intercession is granted.

(p. 405) ﴿And God knows your movement and your resting place﴾. There are three opinions concerning this:

The first: "your movement" in this world and "your resting place" in the Hereafter. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas.

The second: "your movement" through the loins of men into the wombs of women, and "your resting place" in the graves. This was said by Ikrimah.

The third: "your movement" by day, and "your resting place," meaning your shelter, by night. This was said by Muqatil.

God's words: ﴿And those who believe say: "Why has a surah not been sent down?"﴾ The exegetes said: They asked their Lord to send down a surah containing the reward for fighting in the way of God, out of their longing for revelation and their eagerness for holy struggle (jihad). So they said, "Lawla," meaning "Why not?" Abu Malik al-Ashja'i used to say that "la" here is superfluous (silah), so the meaning is: "If only a surah were sent down," out of their longing for an increase in knowledge and their desire for reward and recompense through multiplying the obligations.

Regarding the meaning of "muhkamah" (clear, definitive), there are three opinions. The first: it is the surah in which fighting is mentioned; this was said by Qatadah. The second: it is the surah in which the lawful and the unlawful are mentioned. The third: it is the surah in which there is no abrogated ruling (mansukh, i.e., a ruling superseded by a later one). Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi related these two opinions.

The meaning of His words: ﴿and fighting is mentioned in it﴾ is: holy struggle was made obligatory in it.

Concerning the meaning of "disease" there are two views. The first: hypocrisy (nifaq); this was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and the majority. The second: doubt; this was said by Muqatil.

(p. 406) God's words: ﴿they look at you﴾, meaning they fix their eyes upon you, looking with an intense gaze, as one with fixed eyes looks at the time of death, because they dislike fighting and fear that if they stay behind, their hypocrisy will become evident.

﴿Woe to them﴾. Al-Asma'i said: The meaning of their saying in threat, "Awla laka," is: may what you dislike befall you and draw near to you. Ibn Qutaybah said: This is a warning and a threat. You say to a man, when you intended harm to him and it escaped you, "Awla laka," then you begin and say: ﴿Obedience and honourable speech...﴾. Sibawayh and al-Khalil said: the meaning is: "Obedience and honourable speech would be better." Al-Farra' said: Obedience is well known in the speech of the Arabs; when they are told, "Do such-and-such," they say, "We hear and obey." So God described their speech before the surah was sent down: that they would say, "We hear and obey." But when the command came down, they disliked it. Hibban related to me from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Awla﴾, then He said: ﴿for them﴾, meaning for those among them who believed: ﴿obedience﴾. So "awla" became a warning for whoever disliked it, and He began the statement of obedience with "for them." Our view is that the first reading is the speech of the Arabs, but this (the report of Abu Salih) is not rejected.

Some exegetes mentioned that the speech is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: "Woe to them, that they should obey and speak what is right by agreeing."

God's words: ﴿But when the matter is resolved upon﴾. Al-Hasan said: the matter became serious. Others said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions became earnest in holy struggle, fighting became obligatory, and the matter became binding upon them. The answer to "idha" (when) is omitted; its estimated form is: "But when the matter is resolved upon, they flinched," which the omitted part is indicated by the following: ﴿But if they had been true to God﴾, meaning in their faith and their struggle, ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ than disobedience and aversion.

The second: it means taking charge of the affairs of people (al-wilayah li-umur al-nas), related by al-Qurazi. According to this, ﴿to cause corruption in the land﴾ means by oppression and injustice.

Ya'qub recited "wa-taqta'u" (and you sever) with a fatha on the ta' and the ta' and a light pronunciation of the tá, with the qaf sukun. Then He censured those who desire that, in the verse that follows.

(p-408) What follows this has already been covered [An-Nisa: 82], up to His saying: ﴿Or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ "Am" here means "bal" (rather). The mention of locks is a metaphor, and the intended meaning is that the heart becomes like a locked house to which guidance cannot reach. [Mujahid said]: the ran is lighter than the taba' (seal), the taba' is lighter than the iqfal (lock), and the iqfal is the most severe of all that. Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: Every son of Adam has four eyes: two eyes in his head for his worldly life and what sustains his livelihood, and two eyes in his heart for his religion and what Allah has promised of the unseen. When Allah wills good for a servant, the two eyes in his heart see; and when He wills otherwise, they are obscured. This is His saying: "Or are there locks upon their hearts?"

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels﴾, i.e., they returned to disbelief. Regarding them there are two views. The first: they are the hypocrites, said by Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd. The second: they are the Jews, said by Qatadah and Muqatil. ﴿After guidance had become clear to them﴾, i.e., after the truth had become evident to them. Whoever says they are the Jews says: after (p-409) the description and attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had become clear to them in their scripture. Sawwala means zayyana (adorned/made attractive). ﴿And prolonged hope for them﴾: Abu Amr and Zayd on the authority of Ya'qub recited "wa-umlia lahum" with a damma on the hamza, a kasra on the lam, followed by an open ya'. Ya'qub, except Zayd, and Aban on the authority of Asim, recited likewise, except that they made the ya' sukun. The rest recited with a fatha on the hamza and the lam. The meaning of imla' has already been covered [Al 'Imran: 178; Al-A'raf: 183].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: the matter is that, i.e., that misguidance, by their saying ﴿to those who hated what Allah has sent down﴾. Regarding who these haters are, there are two views.

The first: they are the hypocrites. According to this, regarding His saying ﴿We will obey you in part of the matter﴾ there are three views. The first: in holding back from supporting Muhammad (ﷺ), said by al-Suddi. The second: in inclining towards you and backing you against Muhammad (ﷺ). The third: in apostasy after belief. Al-Mawardi related both of these.

The second: they are the Jews. According to this, regarding that in which they obeyed them, there are two views. The first: in not affirming any of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said by al-Dahhak. The second: in concealing what they knew of his prophethood, said by Ibn Jurayj.

﴿And Allah knows their secrets﴾: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Hafs on the authority of Asim, and al-Walid on the authority of Ya'qub recited with a kasra on the alif, as a masdar of asrartu (I concealed). The rest recited with a fatha on it, as a plural of sirr (secret). The meaning is that He knows the secret matters between the Jews and the hypocrites.

(p-410) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take their souls?﴾, i.e., how will their state be at that time? We have explained the meaning of His saying ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾ in [Al-Anfal: 50].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they hated His pleasure﴾, i.e., they hated that which contains His pleasure, which is faith and obedience.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 47, verse 29–34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring out their malice?﴾ That is, hypocrisy. Al-Farra' said: That is, Allah will not reveal their enmity and hatred toward Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Zajjaj said: That is, He will not reveal their enmity toward His Messenger (ﷺ) and will make their hypocrisy manifest.

(p-411) ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you﴾ That is, We would have made them known to you. You say: "I have shown you this matter," meaning "I have informed you of it." The meaning is: If We willed, We would have placed a mark upon the hypocrites, which is the sign (al-simah). ﴿And you would know them by their sign﴾ That is, by that mark. ﴿And you will surely recognize them by the tone of speech﴾ That is, in the import of the speech. This indicates that a speaker's words and actions reveal his intention. The people's saying "Such-and-such has laHana" (lahana) means that he has taken a course away from what is correct and deviated from the correct toward it. The poet's saying:

"Your speech is sound, but we find you laHnan at times, and the best speech is that which is laHn (allusive)."

Its interpretation: the best speech of this kind is that which not everyone understands, but whose words are recognized only through the subtleties of its expression. The exegetes said: "And you will surely recognize them in the import, meaning and intent of the speech, for they make indirect remarks disparaging your affair and mocking the Muslims." Ibn Jarir said: Then Allah made him know them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will surely test you﴾ That is, We will deal with you as one who tests, by commanding you to jihad, ﴿until We know﴾ the knowledge that is knowledge of existence, upon which reward is based. We have explained this in [al-'Ankabut: 3].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will test your reports﴾ That is, We will make them manifest and expose them through the refusal of whoever refuses to fight and is not patient in jihad. Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, recited: "wa-la-yabluwanna-kum" with ya' and "hatta ya'lama" with ya' and "wa-yabluwa" with ya' in all of them. Mu'adh al-Qari' and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani recited: "akhyarakum" with ya', the plural of "khayyir" (good people) in place of "akhbarakum" (reports).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve...﴾ [the verse]. They differed concerning who it was revealed about, in four opinions.

One: It concerns those who fed (the people) on the day of Badr; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: It was revealed about al-Harith ibn Suwayd and Wahwah al-Ansari, who embraced Islam then apostatized. Al-Harith repented and returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but his companion refused to return until he died; this was said by al-Suddi.

The third: It concerns the Jews; this was said by Muqatil.

The fourth: It concerns Qurayzah [and al-Nadir]; mentioned by al-Wahidi.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not nullify your deeds﴾ They differed concerning what nullifies them, in four opinions. One: sins and major sins; this was said by al-Hasan. The second: doubt and hypocrisy; this was said by 'Ata'. The third: showing off and seeking fame; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib. The fourth: by reminding of favor (al-mann), and that is (p-413) "that some of the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'We came to you willingly, so we have a right over you,' and this verse was revealed, and the saying of Allah was revealed: ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have embraced Islam﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17]," this is the saying of Muqatil. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: This indicates that whoever enters into an act of worship is not permitted to leave it before completing it. This applies literally to Hajj; as for prayer and fasting, it is by way of recommendation.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَلا تَهِنُوا﴾ أيْ: فَلا تَضْعُفُوا ﴿وَتَدْعُوا إلى السَّلْمِ﴾ قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، ونافِعٌ، وأبُو عَمْرٍو، وابْنُ عامِرٍ، والكِسائِيُّ، وحَفْصٌ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: "إلى السَّلْمِ" بِفَتْحِ السِّينِ؛ وقَرَأ حَمْزَةُ، وأبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ: بِكَسْرِ السِّينِ، والمَعْنى: لا تَدْعُوا الكُفّارَ إلى الصُّلْحِ ابْتَداءً. وفي هَذا دَلالَةٌ عَلى أنَّهُ لا يَجُوزُ طَلَبُ الصُّلْحِ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ، ودَلالَةٌ عَلى أنَّ النَّبِيَّ (ﷺ) لَمْ يَدْخُلْ مَكَّةَ صُلْحًا، لِأنَّهُ نَهاهُ عَنِ الصُّلْحِ.

(p-٤١٤) قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَأنْتُمُ الأعْلَوْنَ﴾ أيْ: أنْتُمْ أعَزُّ مِنهُمْ، والحُجَّةُ لَكُمْ، وآخِرُ الأمْرِ لَكم وإنْ غَلَبُوكم في بَعْضِ الأوْقاتِ ﴿واللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ﴾ بِالعَوْنِ والنُّصْرَةِ ﴿وَلَنْ يَتِرَكُمْ﴾ قالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: أيْ: لَنْ يَنْقُصَكم ولَنْ يَظْلِمَكُمْ، يُقالُ: وتَرْتَنِي حَقِّي، أيْ: بَخَسْتَنِيهِ. قالَ المُفَسِّرُونَ: المَعْنى: لَنْ يَنْقُصَكم مِن ثَوابِ أعْمالِكم شَيْئًا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا يَسْألْكم أمْوالَكُمْ﴾ أيْ: لَنْ يَسْألَكُمُوها كُلَّها.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾ قالَ الفَرّاءُ: يُجْهِدْكم. وقالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: يُلِحَّ عَلَيْكم بِما يُوجِبُهُ في أمْوالِكم ﴿تَبْخَلُوا﴾، [يُقالُ: أحْفانِي بِالمَسْألَةِ وألْحَفَ: إذا ألَحَّ. وقالَ السُّدِّيُّ: إنْ يَسْألْكم جَمِيعَ ما في أيْدِيكم تَبْخَلُوا] .

﴿وَيُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ﴾ وقَرَأ سَعْدُ بْنُ أبِي وقّاصٍ، وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، وابْنُ يَعْمَرَ: "وَيُخْرَجُ" بِياءٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ وفَتْحِ الرّاءِ "أضْغانُكُمْ" بِالرَّفْعِ. وقَرَأ أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ، وأبُو رَزِينٍ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وابْنُ السَّمَيْفَعِ، وابْنُ مُحَيْصِنٍ، والجَحْدَرِيُّ: "وَتَخْرُجُ" بِتاءٍ مَفْتُوحَةٍ ورَفْعِ الرّاءِ "أضْغانُكُمْ" بِالرَّفْعِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، والوَلِيدُ عَنْ (p-٤١٥) يَعْقُوبَ: "وَنَخْرِجُ" بِنُونٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ وكَسْرِ الرّاءِ "أضْغانَكُمْ" بِنَصْبِ النُّونِ، أيْ: يُظْهِرُ بُغْضَكم وعَداوَتَكم لِلَّهِ ولِرَسُولِهِ (ﷺ)؛ ولَكِنَّهُ فَرَضَ عَلَيْكم يَسِيرًا.

وَفِيمَن يُضافُ إلَيْهِ هَذا الإخْراجُ وجْهانِ.

أحَدُهُما: إلى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وجَلَّ. والثّانِي: البُخْلُ، حَكاهُما الفَرّاءُ. وقَدْ زَعَمَ قَوْمٌ أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ مَنسُوخَةٌ بِآيَةِ الزَّكاةِ، ولَيْسَ بِصَحِيحٍ، لِأنّا قَدْ بَيَّنّا أنَّ مَعْنى الآيَةِ: إنْ يَسْألْكم جَمِيعَ أمْوالِكُمْ؛ والزَّكاةُ لا تُنافِي ذَلِكَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ها أنْتُمْ هَؤُلاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنْفِقُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ يَعْنِي ما فُرِضَ عَلَيْكم في أمْوَلِكم ﴿فَمِنكم مَن يَبْخَلُ﴾ بِما فُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الزَّكاةِ ﴿وَمَن يَبْخَلْ فَإنَّما يَبْخَلْ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ أيْ: عَلى نَفْسِهِ بِما يَنْفَعُها في الآخِرَةِ ﴿واللَّهُ الغَنِيُّ﴾ عَنْكم وعَنْ أمْوالِكم ﴿وَأنْتُمُ الفُقَراءُ﴾ إلَيْهِ وإلى ما عِنْدَهُ مِنَ الخَيْرِ والرَّحْمَةِ ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ عَنْ طاعَتِهِ ﴿يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ أطْوَعُ لَهُ مِنكم ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أمْثالَكُمْ﴾ بَلْ خَيْرًا مِنكم. وفي هَؤُلاءِ القَوْمِ ثَمانِيَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُمُ العَجَمُ، قالَهُ الحَسَنُ. وفِيهِ حَدِيثٌ يَرْوِيهِ أبُو هُرَيْرَةَ قالَ: «لَمّا نَزَلَتْ ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ كانَ سَلْمانُ إلى جَنْبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ)، فَقالُوا: يا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَن هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ إذا تَوَلَّيْنا اسْتُبْدِلُوا بِنا؟ فَضَرَبَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) [يَدَهُ] عَلى مَنكِبِ سَلْمانَ، فَقالَ: "هَذا وقَوْمُهُ، والَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لَوْ أنَّ الدِّينَ مُعَلَّقٌ بِالثُّرَيّا لَتَناوَلَهُ رِجالٌ مِن فارِسَ" .» والثّانِي: فارِسُ والرُّومُ، قالَهُ (p-٤١٦) عِكْرِمَةُ. والثّالِثُ: مَن يَشاءُ مِن جَمِيعِ النّاسِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والرّابِعُ: يَأْتِي بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ غَيْرِكُمْ، وهو مَعْنى قَوْلِ قَتادَةَ. والخامِسُ: كِنْدَةُ والنَّخَعُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ السّائِبِ. والسّادِسُ: أهْلُ اليَمَنِ، قالَهُ راشِدُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، وعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وشُرَيْحُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ. والسّابِعُ: الأنْصارُ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ. والثّامِنُ: أنَّهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ، حَكاهُ الزَّجّاجُ وقالَ: فِيهِ بُعْدٌ [لِأنَّهُ] لا يُقالُ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ "قَوْمٌ"، إنَّما يُقالُ ذَلِكَ (p-٤١٧) لِلْآدَمِيِّينَ؛ قالَ: وقَدْ قِيلَ: إنْ تَوَلّى أهْلُ مَكَّةَ اسْتَبْدَلَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ أهْلَ المَدِينَةِ، وهَذا [مَعْنى] ما ذَكَرْنا عَنْ مُقاتِلٍ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا يَسْألْكم أمْوالَكُمْ﴾ أيْ: لَنْ يَسْألَكُمُوها كُلَّها.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَيُحْفِكُمْ﴾ قالَ الفَرّاءُ: يُجْهِدْكم. وقالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: يُلِحَّ عَلَيْكم بِما يُوجِبُهُ في أمْوالِكم ﴿تَبْخَلُوا﴾، [يُقالُ: أحْفانِي بِالمَسْألَةِ وألْحَفَ: إذا ألَحَّ. وقالَ السُّدِّيُّ: إنْ يَسْألْكم جَمِيعَ ما في أيْدِيكم تَبْخَلُوا] .

﴿وَيُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ﴾ وقَرَأ سَعْدُ بْنُ أبِي وقّاصٍ، وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، وابْنُ يَعْمَرَ: "وَيُخْرَجُ" بِياءٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ وفَتْحِ الرّاءِ "أضْغانُكُمْ" بِالرَّفْعِ. وقَرَأ أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ، وأبُو رَزِينٍ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وابْنُ السَّمَيْفَعِ، وابْنُ مُحَيْصِنٍ، والجَحْدَرِيُّ: "وَتَخْرُجُ" بِتاءٍ مَفْتُوحَةٍ ورَفْعِ الرّاءِ "أضْغانُكُمْ" بِالرَّفْعِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، والوَلِيدُ عَنْ (p-٤١٥) يَعْقُوبَ: "وَنَخْرِجُ" بِنُونٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ وكَسْرِ الرّاءِ "أضْغانَكُمْ" بِنَصْبِ النُّونِ، أيْ: يُظْهِرُ بُغْضَكم وعَداوَتَكم لِلَّهِ ولِرَسُولِهِ (ﷺ)؛ ولَكِنَّهُ فَرَضَ عَلَيْكم يَسِيرًا.

وَفِيمَن يُضافُ إلَيْهِ هَذا الإخْراجُ وجْهانِ.

أحَدُهُما: إلى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وجَلَّ. والثّانِي: البُخْلُ، حَكاهُما الفَرّاءُ. وقَدْ زَعَمَ قَوْمٌ أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ مَنسُوخَةٌ بِآيَةِ الزَّكاةِ، ولَيْسَ بِصَحِيحٍ، لِأنّا قَدْ بَيَّنّا أنَّ مَعْنى الآيَةِ: إنْ يَسْألْكم جَمِيعَ أمْوالِكُمْ؛ والزَّكاةُ لا تُنافِي ذَلِكَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ها أنْتُمْ هَؤُلاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنْفِقُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ يَعْنِي ما فُرِضَ عَلَيْكم في أمْوَلِكم ﴿فَمِنكم مَن يَبْخَلُ﴾ بِما فُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الزَّكاةِ ﴿وَمَن يَبْخَلْ فَإنَّما يَبْخَلْ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ أيْ: عَلى نَفْسِهِ بِما يَنْفَعُها في الآخِرَةِ ﴿واللَّهُ الغَنِيُّ﴾ عَنْكم وعَنْ أمْوالِكم ﴿وَأنْتُمُ الفُقَراءُ﴾ إلَيْهِ وإلى ما عِنْدَهُ مِنَ الخَيْرِ والرَّحْمَةِ ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ عَنْ طاعَتِهِ ﴿يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ أطْوَعُ لَهُ مِنكم ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أمْثالَكُمْ﴾ بَلْ خَيْرًا مِنكم. وفي هَؤُلاءِ القَوْمِ ثَمانِيَةُ أقْوالٍ.

أحَدُها: أنَّهُمُ العَجَمُ، قالَهُ الحَسَنُ. وفِيهِ حَدِيثٌ يَرْوِيهِ أبُو هُرَيْرَةَ قالَ: «لَمّا نَزَلَتْ ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ كانَ سَلْمانُ إلى جَنْبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ)، فَقالُوا: يا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَن هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ إذا تَوَلَّيْنا اسْتُبْدِلُوا بِنا؟ فَضَرَبَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) [يَدَهُ] عَلى مَنكِبِ سَلْمانَ، فَقالَ: "هَذا وقَوْمُهُ، والَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لَوْ أنَّ الدِّينَ مُعَلَّقٌ بِالثُّرَيّا لَتَناوَلَهُ رِجالٌ مِن فارِسَ" .» والثّانِي: فارِسُ والرُّومُ، قالَهُ (p-٤١٦) عِكْرِمَةُ. والثّالِثُ: مَن يَشاءُ مِن جَمِيعِ النّاسِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ. والرّابِعُ: يَأْتِي بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ غَيْرِكُمْ، وهو مَعْنى قَوْلِ قَتادَةَ. والخامِسُ: كِنْدَةُ والنَّخَعُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ السّائِبِ. والسّادِسُ: أهْلُ اليَمَنِ، قالَهُ راشِدُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، وعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وشُرَيْحُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ. والسّابِعُ: الأنْصارُ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلٌ. والثّامِنُ: أنَّهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ، حَكاهُ الزَّجّاجُ وقالَ: فِيهِ بُعْدٌ [لِأنَّهُ] لا يُقالُ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ "قَوْمٌ"، إنَّما يُقالُ ذَلِكَ (p-٤١٧) لِلْآدَمِيِّينَ؛ قالَ: وقَدْ قِيلَ: إنْ تَوَلّى أهْلُ مَكَّةَ اسْتَبْدَلَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ أهْلَ المَدِينَةِ، وهَذا [مَعْنى] ما ذَكَرْنا عَنْ مُقاتِلٍ.
